issues.legal_issue: Laws placed in the protected constitutional schedule are immune from challenges based on infringement of fundamental rights, including amendments enacted before the parent law was placed there.
material_facts: The landowners challenged legislation that transferred ownership of certain lands to protected tenants, alleging inconsistency with constitutional property rights.
The parent tenancy law and a later re-enactment were placed in the Ninth Schedule by a constitutional amendment.
The amendment that inserted the provision authorising the transfer of ownership had been enacted before the parent law was placed in the Ninth Schedule.
issues.conclusion: The parent law, its amending laws, and the re-enactment were immune from challenge under Articles 19 and 31; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31B protects an Act and its provisions included in the Ninth Schedule from challenges based on inconsistency with or abridgment of rights in Part III, notwithstanding contrary court orders. That protection also covers amending laws enacted before the parent Act was included in the Schedule. The Supreme Court's holding rested on Article 31B and the relevant Ninth Schedule entries; although the High Court had cited Sri Ram Narain v. State of Bombay concerning similar tenancy provisions, the Supreme Court did not rely on that case as the basis for this holding.

rule.if: appeal_from_constitutional_challenge and parent_law_in_protected_schedule and amendment_enacted_before_parent_schedule_entry and challenge_based_on_fundamental_rights

predicates.appeal_from_constitutional_challenge: A party appeals from the dismissal of a proceeding challenging the constitutionality of a law.
predicates.parent_law_in_protected_schedule: The legislature places the parent law in the constitutionally protected schedule.
predicates.amendment_enacted_before_parent_schedule: The legislature enacts an amendment to the parent law before the parent law is placed in the protected schedule.
predicates.challenge_based_on_fundamental_rights: A party alleges that the law or its provisions infringe constitutionally protected fundamental rights.

issues.definition: When an appeal from a constitutional challenge concerns a parent law placed in the protected schedule after an amendment was enacted, and the challenge alleges infringement of fundamental rights, the parent law and covered amendments are immune from that challenge.
